emerging_technology: Passive back-support industrial exoskeletons without electronics or employee tracking.
intended_application: Optional back support during repetitive manual case palletizing at one ground-level warehouse station; no forklift operation, ladders, or increased load limits.
business_need: Evaluate whether a wearable support can improve task comfort after feasible workstation improvements; do not assume injury reduction or productivity gains.
users_stakeholders: Warehouse associates including temporary staff, shift supervisors, safety/ergonomics staff, HR, operations sponsor, maintenance and procurement.
adoption_posture: Moderate fast follower; willing to learn through controlled evaluation, with no mandatory rollout.
risk_consequence_context: Poor fit or restricted movement could create worker discomfort or safety hazards. Worker participation must be voluntary; no higher lifting limits or output quotas. Existing handling aids and stop-work rights remain in force.
management_question: Can this organization absorb, govern and sustain a voluntary station-level evaluation now, and what readiness gaps block it?
time_horizon: Six-week readiness review ending December 21, 2026; any scale decision requires separate evidence and authorization.
additional_context:
All organizations, staffing, budgets and site observations below are fictional scenario assumptions created for assignment testing, not interviews or observed pilot results. Common evidence packet follows.
E1: Industrial Exoskeletons (NIOSH, 2020-01-07); checked 2026-11-09; https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/bulletin/2020/industrial-exoskeletons.html. Support: Task-specific potential benefit; fit, mobility and transferred risks require evaluation; address residual risk after feasible engineering controls. Limit: Older research commentary, not a device certification or proof of long-term injury reduction. Do not treat its research snapshot as the entire 2026 evidence base.
E2: Science and Tech Spotlight Wearable Technologies in the Workplace (US GAO, 2024-03-04); checked 2026-11-09; https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-24-107303. Support: Workplace wearable adoption can face cost and usability barriers; published efficacy evidence is limited. Limit: Broad wearable overview. Sensor privacy issues cannot automatically be attributed to a passive device with no electronics.
E3: About Ergonomics and Work Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (NIOSH, 2024-02-21 (displayed review date)); checked 2026-11-09; https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/ergonomics/about/index.html. Support: Design work and job demands around worker capabilities; evaluate physical and psychosocial risk factors. Limit: General methodological guidance, not a local task assessment or a legal opinion.
capabilities_constraints: Leadership: operations director supports exploration but has not signed a charter or assigned stop authority. Skills: supervisors have no device-fitting or ergonomics training; no retained ergonomist. Workflow: repeat palletizing station has a lift table and rotation, but no documented residual-risk assessment or device SOP. Infrastructure/data: no task baseline, fit inventory, cleaning/storage plan or inspection log. Resources: $4,000 device-purchase allowance only; no paid training/backfill or ongoing service budget. Governance: no trial risk review or documented withdrawal/incident procedure. Culture: workers were not consulted; supervisors want faster throughput. Operating ownership: purchasing owns buying, but nobody owns daily fitting, inspection, cleaning or withdrawal. Worker size compatibility and maintenance support are unknown.
